quests.hint: MAKING SURE NO ONE CAN GET INSIDE WITHOUT A KEY
quests.explanation: LOCK THE DOOR means to secure it so it can't be opened. LOCK pairs with doors, windows, and cars — anything you close and secure with a key or a switch.
quests.instruction: Find the word that naturally completes the pair.
wrongCollocations: close the DOOR with a key turned
shut the DOOR tightly with a lock
quests.contextSentence: Before going to bed, always remember to lock the front ___.

quests.hint: SWITCHING OFF SOMETHING BEFORE YOU LEAVE A ROOM TO SAVE ENERGY
quests.explanation: TURN OFF THE LIGHT means to switch it off. TURN OFF is used for anything powered by electricity — turn off the light, the television, or the computer.
quests.instruction: Choose the word that completes this energy-saving habit.
wrongCollocations: close the LIGHT when leaving
stop the LIGHT switch
quests.contextSentence: As she left the kitchen, she reached back to turn off the ___.

quests.hint: PLACING A JACKET ON A HOOK SO IT DOESN'T LIE ON THE FLOOR
quests.explanation: HANG UP YOUR COAT means to place it on a hook or hanger. HANG UP is also used for phone calls, but with clothing it simply means storing something off the floor.
quests.instruction: Select the word that fits this tidying habit.
wrongCollocations: put up your COAT on the wall
set up your COAT neatly
quests.contextSentence: Please hang up your ___ by the door instead of leaving it on the chair.

quests.hint: EATING YOUR FIRST MEAL OF THE DAY, WHETHER YOU COOKED IT OR NOT
quests.explanation: HAVE BREAKFAST simply means to eat it, regardless of who prepared it. Compare this with MAKE BREAKFAST, which specifically refers to preparing the food.
quests.instruction: Find the word that naturally completes the pair.
wrongCollocations: make BREAKFAST every morning without eating
do BREAKFAST at the table
quests.contextSentence: I never have time to have ___ before work, so I just grab some coffee.

quests.hint: TIPPING A LIQUID FROM A BOTTLE OR JUG INTO A GLASS
quests.explanation: POUR A DRINK describes moving liquid from a container into a cup or glass. POUR is used for any liquid — pour water, pour juice, pour tea.
quests.instruction: Choose the word that completes this everyday action.
wrongCollocations: make a DRINK by tipping a jug
spill a DRINK on purpose
quests.contextSentence: Could you pour me a ___ while you're up? Just water is fine.

quests.hint: REMOVING THE DIRTY PLATES AND GLASSES ONCE EVERYONE HAS FINISHED EATING
quests.explanation: CLEAR THE TABLE is the opposite action of SET THE TABLE — instead of arranging dishes before a meal, you remove them afterward. CLEAR is used whenever you empty a surface of clutter.
quests.instruction: Pick the word that fits this after-dinner task.
wrongCollocations: empty the TABLE of guests
wash the TABLE with plates on it
quests.contextSentence: Once everyone finished eating, the children helped clear the ___.

quests.hint: SITTING DOWN TO ANSWER A SET OF QUESTIONS UNDER TIMED CONDITIONS
quests.explanation: TAKE A TEST means to sit and complete it. TAKE is the general verb for this action, while the result — passing or failing — uses different verbs entirely.
quests.instruction: Find the word that naturally completes the pair.
wrongCollocations: do a TEST sitting silently
make a TEST answer sheet
quests.contextSentence: Nervous students lined up outside the hall to take their final ___.

quests.hint: SPENDING TIME REVIEWING YOUR NOTES BEFORE A BIG SCHOOL ASSESSMENT
quests.explanation: STUDY FOR AN EXAM means to prepare in advance by reviewing material. STUDY FOR is followed by the assessment itself, while STUDY alone can describe learning a subject in general.
quests.instruction: Choose the word that completes this preparation routine.
wrongCollocations: learn for an EXAM by memorizing everything at once
revise an EXAM the night after
quests.contextSentence: She spent the whole weekend in the library studying for her chemistry ___.

quests.hint: GETTING A GOOD ENOUGH SCORE TO SUCCEED, RATHER THAN FAILING
quests.explanation: PASS AN EXAM means to succeed in it, usually by reaching the required score. PASS is the outcome verb, unlike TAKE, which simply describes sitting the exam without saying whether you succeeded.
quests.instruction: Select the word that completes this outcome.
wrongCollocations: win an EXAM by scoring highest
beat an EXAM easily
quests.contextSentence: After weeks of studying, he was relieved to finally pass his driving ___.

quests.hint: CLICKING A SAFETY STRAP ACROSS YOUR BODY BEFORE A CAR STARTS MOVING
quests.explanation: FASTEN YOUR SEATBELT is the standard safety instruction. FASTEN is used for straps and buckles that click into place, unlike TIE, which is used for laces or ropes.
quests.instruction: Find the word that naturally completes the pair.
wrongCollocations: tie your SEATBELT like a shoelace
close your SEATBELT shut
quests.contextSentence: Before starting the engine, the driver reminded everyone to fasten their ___.

quests.hint: LEAVING YOUR VEHICLE STOPPED IN A SPACE, USUALLY FOR A WHILE
quests.explanation: PARK THE CAR means to stop and leave it in a suitable space. PARK is specific to vehicles, unlike STOP, which can apply to any kind of movement.
quests.instruction: Choose the word that completes this driving action.
wrongCollocations: stop the CAR permanently in a spot
rest the CAR overnight
quests.contextSentence: There was nowhere left to park the ___, so we had to circle the block twice.

quests.hint: ADDING FUEL UNTIL A VEHICLE'S CONTAINER IS COMPLETELY FULL
quests.explanation: FILL UP THE TANK means to add fuel until it's full. FILL UP is a phrasal verb specifically used for containers being loaded to capacity, such as a fuel tank or a water bottle.
quests.instruction: Pick the word that fits this refueling stop.
wrongCollocations: fill in the TANK with paperwork
complete the TANK to the top with air
quests.contextSentence: We stopped at the next station to fill up the ___ before the long drive.

quests.hint: CONNECTING A DEVICE TO POWER SO ITS BATTERY FILLS BACK UP
quests.explanation: CHARGE YOUR PHONE means to connect it to power so the battery refills. CHARGE is used for anything with a rechargeable battery — a phone, a laptop, headphones.
quests.instruction: Find the word that naturally completes the pair.
wrongCollocations: fill your PHONE with electricity by hand
power your PHONE with water
quests.contextSentence: My battery was almost dead, so I had to charge my ___ before leaving the house.

quests.hint: PROGRAMMING A DEVICE TO MAKE A SOUND AT A SPECIFIC TIME TO WAKE YOU
quests.explanation: SET AN ALARM means to program it to go off at a chosen time. SET pairs with things you arrange in advance, such as an alarm, a timer, or a reminder.
quests.instruction: Choose the word that completes this bedtime habit.
wrongCollocations: make an ALARM ring by hand
do an ALARM before sleeping
quests.contextSentence: He always sets an ___ for six, even though he usually wakes up earlier.

quests.hint: PUTTING EVERYTHING BACK IN ITS PLACE SO A SPACE LOOKS NEAT AGAIN
quests.explanation: TIDY UP THE HOUSE means to put things back in order throughout the whole home, not just one room. TIDY UP is broader and more casual than CLEAN, which often implies actual washing or scrubbing.
quests.instruction: Select the word that completes this weekend chore.
wrongCollocations: clear up the HOUSE entirely with soap
fix up the HOUSE structurally
quests.contextSentence: Guests were coming over, so they spent the whole morning tidying up the ___.

quests.hint: RECEIVING YOUR MONEY BACK AFTER RETURNING SOMETHING YOU BOUGHT
quests.explanation: GET A REFUND means to receive your money back, usually after returning a faulty or unwanted item. GET pairs with REFUND the way it does with many things you receive rather than create.
quests.instruction: Find the word that naturally completes the pair.
wrongCollocations: make a REFUND happen for yourself
do a REFUND at checkout
quests.contextSentence: The jacket had a hole in it, so she went back to the shop to get a ___.

quests.hint: CHECKING SEVERAL SHOPS TO SEE WHICH ONE CHARGES LESS FOR THE SAME THING
quests.explanation: COMPARE PRICES means to check different sellers before deciding where to buy. COMPARE is used whenever you look at two or more things side by side to judge which is better.
quests.instruction: Choose the word that completes this smart-shopping habit.
wrongCollocations: match PRICES together for fun
count PRICES one by one
quests.contextSentence: Before buying the laptop, he spent an hour online comparing ___ at different stores.

quests.hint: TRANSFERRING MONEY TO SETTLE A BILL, RENT, OR PURCHASE
quests.explanation: MAKE A PAYMENT is the standard way to describe settling a bill or purchase, especially in formal or written contexts. MAKE pairs with PAYMENT much like it does with a decision or an offer.
quests.instruction: Pick the word that fits this financial action.
wrongCollocations: do a PAYMENT online quickly
take a PAYMENT from your account
quests.contextSentence: You can make a ___ online or over the phone using your card details.

quests.hint: SHARING YOUR OPINION ON WHAT SOMEONE SHOULD DO IN A SITUATION
quests.explanation: GIVE ADVICE means to offer your opinion or suggestion to help someone. GIVE pairs with ADVICE the way it does with help or information — things you offer to another person.
quests.instruction: Find the word that naturally completes the pair.
wrongCollocations: make ADVICE for someone else
do ADVICE when asked
quests.contextSentence: My grandmother always gives good ___ about how to handle difficult people.

quests.hint: REQUESTING SOMEONE'S ASSISTANCE WHEN YOU CAN'T MANAGE ON YOUR OWN
quests.explanation: ASK FOR HELP means to request assistance. ASK FOR is followed by the thing you want someone to give you, such as help, advice, or directions.
quests.instruction: Choose the word that completes this everyday request.
wrongCollocations: demand HELP loudly at all times
beg HELP from strangers
quests.contextSentence: If the boxes are too heavy, don't hesitate to ask for ___.

quests.hint: APOLOGIZING OUT LOUD WHEN YOU'VE DONE SOMETHING WRONG
quests.explanation: SAY SORRY is the everyday way to apologize. SAY pairs with short spoken expressions like sorry, hello, or goodbye, while more formal apologies use the verb APOLOGIZE.
quests.instruction: Select the word that completes this polite response.
wrongCollocations: make SORRY to someone politely
give SORRY as a gift
quests.contextSentence: He forgot to say ___ after bumping into the other customer at the store.

quests.hint: ASKING SOMEONE TO JOIN YOU AT AN EVENT OR GATHERING
quests.explanation: INVITE A FRIEND means to ask them to come to something you're hosting. INVITE is used specifically for asking people, unlike ASK, which can apply to questions or requests of any kind.
quests.instruction: Find the word that naturally completes the pair.
wrongCollocations: call a FRIEND over unannounced instead
welcome a FRIEND without asking first
quests.contextSentence: For her birthday, she decided to invite every ___ from her old school.

quests.hint: ORGANIZING A CELEBRATION WITH GUESTS, MUSIC, AND FOOD
quests.explanation: THROW A PARTY means to organize and host one. THROW is an informal but very common verb for hosting a social event, especially in casual, spoken English.
quests.instruction: Choose the word that completes this social event.
wrongCollocations: make a PARTY happen by accident
do a PARTY for no reason
quests.contextSentence: They decided to throw a surprise ___ for their mother's sixtieth birthday.

quests.hint: MARKING A SPECIAL YEARLY OCCASION WITH CAKE, GIFTS, OR A GATHERING
quests.explanation: CELEBRATE A BIRTHDAY means to mark the occasion, often with a party or gathering. CELEBRATE is used broadly for special days — celebrate a birthday, an anniversary, or a holiday.
quests.instruction: Pick the word that fits this special occasion.
wrongCollocations: hold a BIRTHDAY inside a box
make a BIRTHDAY for someone else
quests.contextSentence: The whole family gathered at the restaurant to celebrate grandpa's ninetieth ___.

quests.hint: PUTTING ON HEADPHONES TO ENJOY YOUR FAVORITE SONGS
quests.explanation: LISTEN TO MUSIC is the natural phrase for this leisure activity. LISTEN TO is followed by anything you hear intentionally, such as music, a podcast, or the radio.
quests.instruction: Find the word that naturally completes the pair.
wrongCollocations: hear MUSIC accidentally on the street
watch MUSIC through headphones
quests.contextSentence: On long train journeys, she likes to listen to ___ to pass the time.

quests.hint: FOLLOWING WORDS ON A PAGE TO ENJOY A STORY BEFORE BED
quests.explanation: READ A BOOK is one of the most basic and common collocations in English. READ pairs with anything written — a book, a newspaper, a magazine, a message.
quests.instruction: Choose the word that completes this relaxing habit.
wrongCollocations: watch a BOOK before bed
play a BOOK on the shelf
quests.contextSentence: Every night before falling asleep, he reads a few pages of a ___.

quests.hint: USING BRUSHES AND COLOR TO CREATE AN IMAGE ON CANVAS
quests.explanation: PAINT A PICTURE describes the act of creating an image using paint. PAINT pairs with anything you create using color and a brush, such as a picture, a wall, or a portrait.
quests.instruction: Select the word that completes this creative hobby.
wrongCollocations: do a PICTURE with paint
make a PICTURE by mixing colors only
quests.contextSentence: On Sunday afternoons, she likes to relax by painting a small ___ of the garden.

quests.hint: LOOKING UP WHETHER IT WILL RAIN OR BE SUNNY TOMORROW
quests.explanation: CHECK THE WEATHER means to look up the forecast before making plans. CHECK is used broadly for looking something up to confirm it, such as the weather, the time, or an email.
quests.instruction: Find the word that naturally completes the pair.
wrongCollocations: read the WEATHER out loud from a book
study the WEATHER for an exam
quests.contextSentence: Before packing for the trip, I always check the ___ for the whole week.

quests.hint: DECIDING IN ADVANCE WHERE YOU'LL GO AND WHAT YOU'LL DO ON A JOURNEY
quests.explanation: PLAN A TRIP means to organize the details of a journey ahead of time — where to go, what to see, and how to get there. PLAN pairs with anything you prepare or organize before it happens.
quests.instruction: Choose the word that completes this preparation activity.
wrongCollocations: make a TRIP before deciding anything
do a TRIP without any thought
quests.contextSentence: They spent the whole evening planning their summer ___ to the coast.

quests.hint: TAKING PLEASURE IN SOMETHING YOU'RE EATING, RATHER THAN RUSHING THROUGH IT
quests.explanation: ENJOY A MEAL means to take pleasure in eating it, often slowly and without rushing. ENJOY is used broadly for anything you take pleasure in — a meal, a book, a holiday.
quests.instruction: Pick the word that completes this simple pleasure.
wrongCollocations: make a MEAL joyful by force
do a MEAL with pleasure only
quests.contextSentence: Instead of eating in front of the television, they sat down to enjoy a proper ___ together.
